# Innovators from the 2025 National Institute on Aging (NIA) Startup Challenge

Innovators from the 2025 National Institute on Aging (NIA) Startup Challenge - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[Innovators from the 2025 National Institute on Aging (NIA) Startup Challenge](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=onQU7-SQysk) [Positive Aging Community](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCJXF33z-rInVElY1bDlt29Q)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/Qh0j8z1NqDKuj-2QD0TrkjWkiXkSA0UPwZMSasqs66HquCxTo7P5KRAw4IA3h3ZSw8y3cdPXQHw=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

* * *

In a rapidly aging world, where the growth of older adults is reshaping societies and economies, innovation isn't just welcome—it's essential. The National Institute on Aging (NIA) Startup Challenge and Accelerator, now in its 2025 edition, is fueling this transformation. From 300 applicants nationwide, 21 standout companies were selected for their groundbreaking work in devices, digital health, and activity-promoting tools. Hosted by the NIA's Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) program, the accelerator provides funding, mentorship, and networking to bridge the gap between cutting-edge ideas and real-world impact. Learn more about the program [here](https://www.nia.nih.gov/research/sbir/startup-challenge/about-challenge-accelerator).

On a recent episode of the _Positive Aging Community_ podcast, host Steve Gurney sat down with four of these trailblazers: Kareem Elfoulie of Senior Shield Technologies, Marie Brodsky of WISE Connect, Neal Shah of CareYaya, and Stefano Selorio of Carevocacy. What emerged was a tapestry of personal stories, disruptive solutions, and shared optimism about dismantling the stigmas and barriers of aging. These entrepreneurs, many drawing from their own family caregiving experiences, are reimagining dignity, connection, and affordability for older adults. Here's a spotlight on their work.

[**Listen on your favorite podcast platform**](https://open.spotify.com/episode/6BIMXeOWObBH54thvus4UE?si=jDvEL8CRQ9KZsOCumVLS_A)

## Senior Shield Technologies: Dignity Through Smarter Incontinence Care

Kareem Elfoulie, CEO and co-founder of Senior Shield Technologies, brings a mechanical engineering background from Georgia Tech and over a decade as a care partner to his mission. His company's flagship product is an incontinence monitoring pad that goes on the outside of any adult brief and sends a digital alert to caregivers when there is a urine or stool accident.

The goal is to promote quicker changes to restore dignity and slash infection risks. Incontinence affects millions, yet it's shrouded in embarrassment, leading to isolation and health crises. Elfoulie highlighted stark stats: People with incontinence face 60% higher fall risks, with eight in 10 falls occurring in bathrooms from rushed trips. Untreated urinary tract infections (UTIs) can spiral into sepsis, costing up to $7,000 per round of antibiotics and up to $68,000 in hospital treatment.

"People's briefs are not getting changed quick enough, and people aren't admitting that there is an actual incontinence problem," Elfoulie said. Fecal incontinence, the No. 2 reason for nursing home admissions, exacerbates this. Senior Shield targets Medicare/Medicaid coverage to make it accessible, reframing a taboo issue as a solvable hygiene win. As Elfoulie put it, "We're not letting people be left behind."

For website and contact info, please use the following links: [www.seniorshieldtech.com](http://www.seniorshieldtech.com/) Email: [kareem.elfoulie@seniorshieldtech.com](mailto:kareem.elfoulie@seniorshieldtech.com)

## WISE Connect: Bridging Isolation with Local, Low-Key Engagement

Marie Brodsky, CEO and co-founder of WISE Connect, believes our communities should be equipped to support us all as we age. She brings experience in age-friendly communities, previously serving on Longevity Ready Maryland, and brings business acumen from intensive programs such as the Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center.

But her story began with seeing her grandfather’s experience of isolation. He felt like there was nothing out there for him, so he stayed home, alone, disconnected. Brodsky set out to change that, for him and millions more. Now, WISE Connect enables older adults to stay active, socially connected and supported at every stage in their own communities.

On the ground, WISE Connect partners with local businesses: Think breweries hosting morning board games and coffee for 20 older adults, or cafes turning quiet hours into info sessions about local senior programs. “Many places have times of the day where there’s not much going on, and it's a perfect opportunity to welcome people in.”

Their free website designed for older adults surfaces these events, making discovery easy. Plus, the website consolidates information about local activities, programs, and services of all kinds for older adults – ranging from walking groups to home modifications. Curious to learn more? Check out [www.wisecities.us](http://www.wisecities.us/). If you’re a business, contact [marie@wiseconnect.us](mailto:marie@wiseconnect.us) to learn more about getting vetted and highlighted through WISE Connect’s website and events.

## CareYaya: Affordable Care via Intergenerational Matchmaking

Neal Shah, CEO and co-founder of CareYaya, pivoted from a high-stakes hedge fund career after grueling caregiving stints for his grandfather (dementia) and wife (cancer). Now mid-career and "a little bit older," Shah's tech-enabled marketplace connects over 50,000 healthcare students—pre-meds, nursing majors—from 30+ universities to older adults needing companionship care, especially for dementia.

In markets like D.C., traditional agencies charge $40–45/hour, paying caregivers half while families foot $80,000+ annually amid shortages and inflation-tripling costs. CareYaya flips the script: $20–25/hour for vetted students, with zero platform fees—all money flows to caregivers. "It's literally mathematically the most affordable care in America," Shah said, backed by rigorous vetting and high ratings.

The magic? Intergenerational bonds. "Mom, Sarah from Georgetown is here—she's going to help you, but you're going to mentor her for her future clinical career," Shah reframed for resistant families. Students gain purpose amid exam stress; seniors share wisdom, combating mutual loneliness. "This creates a lot of purpose and meaning, which benefits both sides," he added. With 2030 looming—when over-65s outnumber under-18s—Shah warns of a "broken" financing system but sees CareYaya as crisis-avoidance: scalable, low-margin volume over VC-chasing niches.

## Carevocacy: Digital Literacy Without the Eye Rolls

In 2020, Stefano Selorio launched Carevocacy, a learning platform that helps lifelong learners be tech-savvy. Carevocacy's latest product, Apo, is a text-based digital health literacy coach powered by AI.

Carevocacy has served over 23,000 Learners across 30 learning locations and has worked with Medicare Advantage plans like Humana, senior living communities, and value-based care clinics.

He is also a caregiver to his grandma, who was diagnosed with Alzheimer's and recently became one of Forbes' 30 Under 30. At 26 years old, Stefano is an avid community builder, a pragmatic optimist, and passionate about creating solutions that meet people where they're at.

## A Collaborative Future: Affordability, Equity, and Urgency

These four aren't siloed stars—they're puzzle pieces. WISE Connect feeds socially engaged seniors to CareYaya caregivers; Apo AI eases tech fears for platform sign-ups; Senior Shield prevents dignity-eroding infections that sideline community involvement. All prioritize affordability and equity, "We're not letting people be left behind," Elfoulie summed up, echoing the cohort's immigrant-rooted ethos.

The NIA's moonshot funding is the spark; these founders are the fire. As the growth of older adults evolves from punchline to priority, expect more cross-pollination, bolder messaging, and real relief. It's reshaping with innovators like these at the helm.
